channel.title: The Melbourne Indian
channel.description: Independent, free-to-read news for Melbourne's Indian communities in English, Hindi and Punjabi.

item.title: Victorian election: who is standing in the seven districts with the most India-born residents
item.description: Nominations have closed. Here are all 60 candidates standing in Tarneit, Laverton, Kalkallo, Point Cook, Cranbourne, Williamstown and Thomastown, and how to fill in your ballot papers.

item.title: Vandals cut power to a temple in Melbourne's west on the eve of Diwali, MPs say
item.description: The SMVS Swaminarayan temple near Tarneit lost power twice in eight days, according to MPs from both major parties. Labor has pledged $200,000 for its security if re-elected.

item.title: Big Build royal commission opens public hearings, starting with a 2022 Sunbury rail shutdown
item.description: The inquiry has sought more than 110,000 documents, counsel assisting said. Its first two-week block of hearings runs until 20 November, eight days before Victorians vote.

item.title: Family visiting from India? Visa applicants there may now need to give fingerprints
item.description: Since 26 October, people applying for an Australian visa in India may be asked for fingerprints and a facial image. The Australian High Commission says applications lodged before that date are not affected.

item.title: India is now Australia's largest overseas-born community
item.description: About 971,000 people living in Australia were born in India, narrowly ahead of England, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

item.title: New student visa rules: who can still apply from inside Australia
item.description: Since 2 October, most temporary visa holders in Australia can no longer lodge a Student visa application onshore, and new applicants generally cannot include a partner or children. Here is what the Department of Home Affairs says has changed.

item.title: Voting help in Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil and more: who to call before 28 November
item.description: The Victorian Electoral Commission has dedicated phone lines for Tamil, Urdu and Nepali speakers. For Hindi, Punjabi, Gujarati, Malayalam and other languages, there is one number to call.

item.title: After the Melbourne summit, where does the India–Australia trade deal stand?
item.description: Leaders agreed in Melbourne in July to move faster on a comprehensive economic agreement. Trade ministers met again in October, but no date has been set to finish the deal.

item.title: International student numbers for 2027: what Indian students in Melbourne need to know
item.description: The federal government has kept the planning level for new international students at 295,000 for 2027, unchanged from this year.

item.title: Little India in Docklands: where Melbourne's precinct plan stands
item.description: The City of Melbourne has set aside more than $1.2 million to develop a Little India precinct in Docklands, but no site has been chosen and many local residents have urged caution.

item.title: Indian passport, visa and OCI services in Melbourne: what changed in 2026
item.description: Indian consular applications in Victoria now go through a VFS Global centre on St Kilda Road, with a $115 service charge per application on top of government fees.

item.title: Diwali 2026: Melbourne marks the festival of lights
item.description: Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November this year. Celebrations across the city began a week earlier.

item.title: Missed this year's multicultural grants? What ran in 2026, and how to be ready next time
item.description: Three Victorian Government funding rounds for multicultural groups and businesses have closed. Here is what they offered, so your organisation can plan ahead.

item.title: Victoria votes on 28 November: the dates you need to know
item.description: Early voting opens on 18 November and postal vote applications close on 25 November. Here is how to vote, and where to get help in your language.

item.title: Welcome to The Melbourne Indian
item.description: A free news service for Melbourne's Indian communities, in English, Hindi and Punjabi.
